newsitem.title: CHINA: China passes law on army garrison for Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China passes law on army garrison for Hong Kong.

text.p: China's parliament on Monday passed a law to cover stationing of People's Liberation Army troops in Hong Kong after it returns to Chinese sovereignty next year, banning soldiers from doing business in the freewheeling city.
The law was passed by the standing committee of the National People's Congress, or parliament, and contained several revisions, the Xinhua news agency said.

Under the revisions, Chinese People's Liberation Army troops will be required to be responsible not only for both the public and private property of Hong Kong and its residents but for the property of non-residents.

The military personnel "shall take good care of the public property of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the private property owned by Hong Kong residents as well as other people", Xinhua said.
The previous version did not specify responsibility for non-Hong Kong people.

The law also carried stricter stipulations to prevent troops and military personnel from engaging in profit-making businesses in the British colony that reverts to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on June 30, 1997, Xinhua said.
As regards judicial powers over the troops, soldiers will be tried by Chinese military courts for offences committed while on duty but crimes off-duty will be handled in Hong Kong.
No other details were immediately available.
